nodes.body: @xinyu-intel Can you explain more about `torch.compile should already handle this`? Previous change is decided mainly to keep same handle process vs cuda path and avoid accuracy issue in some corner cases, I remember also related with `torch.compile`?

Without an out-of-place copy, this causes an all-zero-accuracy issue under torch.compile — see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39844.

If we really want to use inplace allreduce, we may need to rely on an environment variable or some other mechanism to determine whether inplace is actually safe to use here. torch.compiler.is_compiling() doesn't work when use custom op all_reduce.

> Without an out-of-place copy, this causes an all-zero-accuracy issue under torch.compile — see #39844.
> 
> If we really want to use inplace allreduce, we may need to rely on an environment variable or some other mechanism to determine whether inplace is actually safe to use here. torch.compiler.is_compiling() doesn't work when use custom op all_reduce.

you're right. we should check eager mode here. but at this point, compilation_config is not available and a WA is to check is_breakable_cudagraph_enabled.
close as it will cause wrong correctness and even race conditions when the input is also the consumer of other operators.

detail.title: [XPU] inplace all_reduce under eager graph mode

files.patch:
@@ -7,6 +7,7 @@
 from torch.distributed import ProcessGroup
 
 import vllm.envs as envs
+from vllm.distributed.device_communicators.utils import is_breakable_cudagraph_enabled
 from vllm.logger import init_logger
 
 from .base_device_communicator import DeviceCommunicatorBase
@@ -65,9 +66,14 @@ def all_reduce(self, input_: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
             # and accumulate in rank order, independent of the token batch.
             return self._fixed_rank_sum(input_)
 
-        output = input_.clone()
-        dist.all_reduce(output, group=self.device_group)
-        return output
+        # should check eager mode, but cannot access compilation_config here.
+        if is_breakable_cudagraph_enabled():
+            dist.all_reduce(input_, group=self.device_group)
+            return input_
+        else:
+            output = input_.clone()
+            dist.all_reduce(output, group=self.device_group)
+            return output
 
     def reduce_scatter(self, input_: torch.Tensor, dim: int = -1):
         world_size = self.world_size
